articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence llega por fin a Instagram con una condición: "Si alguien dice algo negativo, me voy"
articles.standfirst: La actriz ha abierto su primera cuenta pública en Instagram, bajo el nombre @jlaw, después de años alejada de las redes sociales
articles.summary: La actriz ha abierto su primera cuenta pública en Instagram, bajo el nombre @jlaw, después de años alejada de las redes sociales
articles.body: Jennifer Lawrence ya está en Instagram. La actriz, que durante años se ha mantenido alejada de las redes sociales, ha abierto finalmente una cuenta pública en la plataforma bajo el nombre de usuario @jlaw. Su desembarco no ha podido ser más fiel a su personalidad: en su primer 'Reel' ha aprovechado para establecer las reglas de su nueva presencia digital. La principal condición es sencilla: nada de comentarios negativos. "Y si alguien dice algo negativo, voy a dejar Instagram inmediatamente", bromea Lawrence en el vídeo. Pero la actriz ha ido un paso más allá y ha advertido a sus seguidores de que ni siquiera será necesario que escriban algo desagradable para que ella lo perciba: "Si alguien piensa algo malo... lo voy a saber". Una amenaza en tono de humor que deja claro que la permanencia de Jennifer Lawrence en Instagram dependerá, al menos según sus propias palabras, del comportamiento de sus seguidores. La llegada de Jennifer Lawrence a Instagram también ha dejado una pequeña curiosidad. La actriz no ha podido utilizar el nombre más evidente, @jenniferlawrence, porque ya estaba ocupado. Ella misma lo explica en la biografía de su perfil con un escueto: "jenniferlawrence estaba tomado". Jennifer Lawrence no ha explicado públicamente qué la ha llevado a abrir ahora una cuenta en Instagram después de tantos años sin una presencia oficial en la plataforma. Sin embargo, su llegada coincide con una etapa profesional especialmente activa, con varios proyectos en el horizonte. Entre ellos destaca 'What Happens at Night', la nueva película dirigida por Martin Scorsese, en la que la actriz comparte protagonismo con Leonardo DiCaprio. El proyecto supone el reencuentro de ambos intérpretes después de 'Don’t Look Up'. La película sigue a una pareja estadounidense que viaja a un pequeño pueblo europeo cubierto de nieve para adoptar a un bebé. Lo que comienza como un viaje aparentemente normal irá adquiriendo tintes cada vez más extraños. El reparto se completa, entre otros, con Mads Mikkelsen, Patricia Clarkson y Jared Harris. Jennifer Lawrence ya ha terminado el rodaje de la película, por lo que su llegada a Instagram podría resultar especialmente oportuna de cara a la futura campaña promocional y al correspondiente tour de prensa junto a Leonardo DiCaprio. La lista de cuentas a las que sigue Jennifer Lawrence también ha despertado curiosidad. Entre sus primeros 'follows' aparecen algunos de sus compañeros y colaboradores de 'What Happens at Night', como Leonardo DiCaprio y Martin Scorsese, además de Josh Hutcherson, con quien compartió protagonismo en 'Los Juegos del Hambre'. También sigue a algunas de sus amigas y compañeras de profesión, entre ellas Dakota Johnson, Amy Schumer y Amy Poehler. Pero la actriz también ha demostrado que sabe perfectamente qué ofrece Instagram en materia de entretenimiento. Entre sus primeras cuentas seguidas están Kim, Khloé y Kourtney Kardashian, Kendall y Kylie Jenner y Kris Jenner. Tras su inesperado desembarco en Instagram, las expectativas sobre lo que Lawrence pueda compartir son altas. Sus seguidores esperan especialmente vídeos en los que la actriz muestre su habitual sentido del humor, además de fotografías de sus viajes, momentos cotidianos y reacciones a acontecimientos virales. También hay interés por los contenidos relacionados con sus próximos proyectos. Los rodajes, los camerinos, los viajes y, sobre todo, el futuro tour de prensa de 'What Happens at Night' podrían convertirse en una fuente de material especialmente atractiva para sus seguidores. Y es que la combinación de Jennifer Lawrence, Leonardo DiCaprio y Martin Scorsese promete generar más de un momento memorable delante y detrás de las cámaras. Por ahora, sin embargo, hay una prioridad para quienes quieran disfrutar de la nueva cuenta de Instagram de la actriz: no hacer enfadar a Jennifer Lawrence. Después de años esperando verla en Instagram, sus seguidores ya conocen la única condición para que @jlaw se quede: "Si alguien dice algo negativo, voy a dejar Instagram inmediatamente".

articles.body: Las carreras de los futbolistas son efímeras y deben buscar la forma de seguir generando un colchón económico una vez que el césped se acaba. Leo Messi vive sus últimos años en el Inter Miami. Ya retirado de la selección argentina después del último Mundial 2026, los expertos son conscientes de que sólo resta una cantidad de encuentros muy pequeña para disfrutar del astro. Cuando Messi cuelgue las botas, uno de los negocios que tiene en marcha es Hincha. Este restaurante tiene locales en Andorra y Sotogrande. Lo creó junto al chef con estrella Michelin Nandu Jubany. Entre sus platos más destacados están sus recetas favoritas de la infancia, como los macarrones de su abuela, la Burger 10 o el postre con forma del Balón de Oro. El creador de contenido Pabloovfyt ha querido comprobar de primera mano cómo es este establecimiento. Ha compartido todas las imágenes en su cuenta de TikTok: “Tenía muy buena pinta. Nos habían recomendado pedir los macarrones de la abuela de Messi y la pizza carbonara”. “De entrante nos traían un pan con aceitunas y, como dato curioso, todos los camareros llevan el pie de Messi a la espalda”, relata sobre sus primeros momentos en el restaurante Hincha. El creador de contenido valora positivamente los macarrones de la abuela, aunque describe como “lo más importante” el postre con forma de Balón de Oro. “Todo estaba buenísimo. Nos dijeron que había que romperlo dándole un pequeño toque arriba pero estaba mucho más duro de lo que esperaba”, comenta sobre este dulce. Al final, bromeaba con “la multa” que le iba a costar todos estos platos: 97,5 euros para dos personas. “Muy bien, se come increíble”, zanja Pablo.

articles.title: Lidia Santos, camarera de 'First Dates', se enamora a primera vista de un soltero: "Me caso"
articles.standfirst: No obstante, el hombre prefirió la cita en el programa de Mediaset con otra chica
articles.summary: No obstante, el hombre estaba en plena cita en el programa de Mediaset con otra chica
articles.body: ‘First Dates’, programa de Mediaset que se emite en Telecinco cada día entre semana a partir de las 21:45 horas, abre las puertas a miles de solteros para encontrar el amor. En cada entrega, suelen acudir dos personas para ver si siguen adelante románticamente hablando o simplemente queda en amistad o en nada. Sin embargo, en una de las últimas emisiones, Lidia Santos, la camarera del programa de citas que presenta y dirige Carlos Sobera, se quedó totalmente “impactada” al ver a un hombre que fue al programa. Santos reveló que le gustaba la gente alta, mostrando interés por el hombre, hasta el punto que Sobera también se quedó ‘a cuadros’: “Hacía tiempo que nadie le removía nada por dentro". Además, Marisa y Cristina, sus compañeras en las comandas también bromearon al respecto y le cuestionaron sobre si le había gustado, a lo que contestó Santos: “Sí, me pareció mono”. Del mismo modo, la propia Lidia y sus dos compañeras alegaron que “el físico no lo es todo” y que tendría que conocerlo antes de lanzar las campanas al vuelo. Sin embargo, Lidia Santos se quedó “impactada” al ver al hombre tan alto, algo que justificó así: “Pero es verdad que de altura me venía muy bien". Eso sí, después de admitir que se había quedado impresionada por su planta e imagen, tan solo le quedaba conocerlo de cerca, pero no podía hablar con él porque estaba en otra cita con otra chica. Sin embargo, Cristina le respondió con la siguiente reflexión: “Si tuviera lo mismo de alto que de cabeza y corazón le ganaría al instante”. Para finalizar, entre carcajadas, Lidia Santos dijo lo siguiente: “Seguro que sí. Entonces me caso”.

articles.body: Shobhaa De has made it clear that the ‘Mirzapur’ universe did little to win her over. The veteran columnist, who revealed that she had never watched the hit Amazon Prime Video crime thriller, recently decided to give its theatrical spin-off, Gurmeet Singh’s ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’, a chance. However, despite the film’s strong box-office run, she came away far from impressed.Sharing her review in an Instagram Reel on Thursday, Shobhaa said she questioned the need for the film after watching it.“All I can say is Mirzapur: The Movie maybe should not have been made at all,” said Shobhaa De. She admitted that she went into the film expecting more after seeing the hype surrounding the franchise. “I went here with a lot of expectations, given the whole hype and the whole buildup to the brand Mirzapur. I came away feeling, ‘What the hell is going on?,’” she added, accompanied by an eyeroll.While the film itself failed to impress her, Shobhaa had praise for its ensemble cast. She singled out Ravi Kishan and Ali Fazal for their performances, calling Kishan’s turn as antagonist Babban Babua Yadav “brilliant” and Fazal’s portrayal of Guddu “unbelievably good”.However, she was less enthusiastic about Pankaj Tripathi’s Kaleen Bhaiya. “Mr. Tripathi playing Mr. Tripathi has become a bit too monotonous,” she said. Shobhaa further criticised what she saw as a repetitive performance, adding, “The same old expressions, the same old delivery.”She was also taken aback by Tripathi’s intimate scenes with Rasika Dugal, who plays his wife Beena Tripathi. Referring to Tripathi as “Mr. Goodie-Goodie”, Shobhaa said she was surprised to see him doing “a full-on sex scene”. She described Beena as “Lady Macbeth” or a “vamp-ish” character.Her other complaints included what she called “violence of every conceivable kind for no reason” and “a story that goes nowhere”. The film apparently struggled to hold her attention too, as she confessed to falling asleep during the screening.Shobhaa said she felt asleep for “something like 15 minutes” and claimed she also heard two women sitting behind her “snoring”. Summing up her experience, she said, “Maybe, it’s meant for men. It wasn’t meant for me.”In the caption accompanying her Reel, Shobhaa wrote, "I spent 900 rupees on the ticket, 260 rupees on bhel, and close to 4 hours wondering why i was watching a movie which had multiple set pieces randomly strung together. I mean...come on ...the dwarf? Camel's milk? A menacing villain who stitches sexy bralets for his "love" ?"‘Mirzapur: The Movie’, which released on September 4, is the big-screen continuation of the popular crime franchise. articles.title: Rick Springfield recalls killing a man in Vietnam while he was there performing for troops
articles.summary: Rocker Rick Springfield recalled this week how, as a teenager, when he performed for U.S. forces in Vietnam, they came under attack and he killed a Viet Cong — haunting him to this day that he “was responsible for the end of a life.”
articles.body: Rocker Rick Springfield recalled this week how, as a teenager, when he performed for U.S. forces in Vietnam, they came under attack and he killed a Viet Cong — haunting him to this day that he “was responsible for the end of a life.” The Australian singer-songwriter became an ‘80s superstar with his megahit “Jessie’s Girl,” but in 1968 he was an unknown 17-year-old musician who had traveled to Southeast Asia to entertain American troops at the height of the Vietnam War. Springfield, 77, recounted that harrowing experience on an episode of the “Joe Rogan Experience” posted on Tuesday. He said he was staying at a U.S. Navy encampment in the Marble Mountains near Da Nang when they suddenly came under attack. “We met these guys, and we really got along well, and we stayed overnight with them, and we all got in the bunkers, in the perimeter bunkers, and I stayed in the radio shack,” he recalled. “And we got attacked, and I’m throwing mortars down the freaking tube of the radio shack.” In the heat of the moment, Springfield said he was haphazardly loading a launcher and “could have easily lost a hand.” “It was like the movies,” he told Rogan. “They said, ‘Hey, you want to throw some mortars down the tube?’ And it was John Wayne time, you know. I mean, as a young kid, I didn’t really understand what I was doing.” But what began like a scene from an action film gave way to the cold, hard realities of war. “I’d thrown a mortar down and it had hit somebody, and they came in the next day and said, ‘Hey, you got one! You got one!’” Springfield said. “That’s really the one thing I brought back with me that I couldn’t really find a place for that to land,” he said, saying that it feels like it happened to “another guy” in “another place.” Rogan asked, “How long did that sit with you for?” and Springfield said the experience has never left him. “I think it’s still there,” Springfield replied. “It’s hard for me to face that I was responsible for the end of a life, even though it’s distant and it’s war and I didn’t really have anything to do with it and didn’t really know what I was doing.” Springfield also vividly recalled how unpopular the war was with the Americans fighting it in Vietnam. “All the ones I met were, ‘Dude, I don’t know why we’re here. I don’t know what I’m doing here,’” he remembered. The “Love Somebody” and “Don’t Talk to Strangers” singer wrote about the Vietnam incident in his 2010 memoir, “Late, Late at Night.” “That was a war situation but it is still something that to this day sends a shiver down my spine,” Springfield wrote in the memoir.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Ex-Wife Justine Claims He Refers to the Mothers of His 14 Children as ‘Breeders’
articles.summary: The Tesla founder welcomed son Nevada Alexander, who died at 10 weeks old, twins Vivian and Griffin and triplets Kai, Saxon and Damian, with his ex-wife
articles.body:
Justine Wilson claims Elon Musk referred to the mothers of his 14 children as "breeders" in a new documentary

Wilson, Musk's first wife, claims he taught her the term "gaslighting" and called himself the "alpha" in their relationship

Musk and his legal team have criticized the documentary, calling it biased and threatening legal action against its creators

Elon Musk 's ex-wife Justine Wilson opened up about her experience during their relationship.

In Alex Gibney's new documentary Musk , which is set to be released on Oct. 16, Wilson claimed that the Tesla founder, 55, referred to the mothers of his 14 children as "breeders." Wilson, who was married to Musk from 2000 to 2008 and welcomed six children with him, said that for the tech mogul, "the breeders are interchangeable."

Elsewhere in the documentary, Wilson, 54, claimed that Musk told her that he was the "alpha" in their relationship while they were dancing at their wedding. She also credited her ex-husband for teaching her the meaning of the term "gaslighting" because of the way he treated her.

"I learned the term 'gaslighting' through my relationship with Elon," Wilson said in the documentary, noting that Musk would make her feel "insignificant" in their marriage.

Wilson and the Tesla founder are parents to twins Vivian and Griffin and triplets Kai, Saxon and Damian. They also shared son Nevada Alexander, who died at 10 weeks old.

Vivian, who is transgender, is referenced in the film. Musk previously said that he lost his daughter to the "woke mind virus."

In the documentary, Wilson said that her ex cut off Vivian's health insurance after she came out as trans and claimed he has "never tried to repair things" with his daughter. She added, "It's not in his nature."

However, Wilson alleged that Elon told her to tell Vivian that "I'll always love her."

Musk himself did not participate in the making of the documentary. In 2023, he denounced the doc as a "hit piece" on X. Responding in another post , Gibney wrote, "How would you know?"

The businessman's attorney Alex Spiro also threatened legal action over the new documentary, alleging that the film falsely suggests Musk manipulated the 2024 presidential election . Spiro sent Gibney a letter ahead of the documentary's release, PEOPLE has learned.

In the letter, Spiro claims Musk's legal team repeatedly attempted to contact Gibney and requested an opportunity to respond to the film's reporting, but alleges that the filmmakers "have refused to engage." Spiro also accuses the filmmakers of allegedly approaching the project with a predetermined conclusion about Musk.

"This project did not begin as an inquiry," Spiro wrote. "It began with a conclusion."

In response, a spokesperson for the production company behind the film, Jigsaw, defended Gibney's work.

"Alex Gibney's films are consistently recognized for their in-depth, fact-driven explorations of influential figures and corporations, coupled with his bold and engaging directorial style," the spokesperson said.

The spokesperson for the documentary's production company did not specifically respond to Spiro's criticism about how Starlink was represented.

"The right to engage in open debate and fact-based examinations of powerful public figures is protected by the First Amendment — something that should be recognized and defended by all Americans, including the associates of Elon Musk, who has proclaimed himself to be a 'free speech absolutist,' " the spokesperson said.

In April 2025, a report from the Wall Street Journal shared that Musk views his children as a "legion," a word that refers to a military unit used by the Roman army that consisted of thousands of soldiers .

"To reach legion-level before the apocalypse, we will need to use surrogates," the SpaceX and Tesla CEO allegedly texted Ashley St. Clair while she was pregnant with their child, who was born in 2025 . (In another nod to Rome, the newspaper reported that their son is named Romulus , who, according to legend , founded the city with his twin brother Remus, then murdered him after an argument.)

The newspaper also alleged in its report that Musk has used X, the social media platform formerly known as Twitter that he purchased in 2022, to try and find more women to have his babies.

In response to the report, published on Tuesday, April 15, Musk tweeted, " TMZ >> WSJ. "

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

In addition to his six children with Wilson and one with St. Clair, Musk also welcomed seven children with two other women. In 2020, two years after Musk and singer Grimes were first linked, the two announced the arrival of their first child, X Æ A-12, together. The former couple share two more children, daughter Exa Dark Sideræl and son Techno Mechanicus.

A few weeks prior to the arrival of their second child, the tech CEO also secretly fathered Strider and Azure with Zilis , an executive at one of his companies, Neuralink, in November 2021, according to court documents published by Business Insider . The pair then welcomed daughter Arcadia in February 2024. Zilis announced that she and Musk had secretly welcomed their fourth child together , son Seldon Lycurgus, in 2025.

articles.body: 'El Hormiguero' ha cerrado la primera semana de su 21ª temporada con la visita este jueves de Ester Expósito una de las actrices más destacadas de su generación y una intérprete con una trayectoria incontestable que a sus 26 años ha conseguido conquistar tanto el mundo del cine como el de las series. A ella la idea en un principio no le gusta nada, pero poco a poco se va enamorando de él y además ve cómo le puede enseñar a defenderse. Ella es la que se lanza a por él y eso me gusta mucho. Es un poco el paso de niña a mujer de mi personaje, y eso es muy chulo. PABLO MOTOS. El coprotagonista, Hugo Diego, te enseña a defenderte en la serie, ¿qué cosas te enseñó? ESTER EXPÓSITO. Sí, me enseñó muchas cosas porque el boxea de verdad, ha sido coach de boxeo. Me enseñó el mataleón, muchas llaves... Me gustó mucho el boxeo y, además, nos sirvió para construir la química entre nuestros personajes PABLO MOTOS. ¿Creo que de más jovencita te llamaban el pitbull? ESTER EXPÓSITO. En la película a tu personaje le secuestran, ¿en la vida real te han atracado alguna vez? ESTER EXPÓSITO. Sí, con una amiga, con 16 años. Estábamos paseando por Chamberí en Madrid. Eran una pareja, nos acorralaron y les dimos los móviles y todo lo que llevábamos. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Has sufrido por amor? ESTER EXPÓSITO. He sufrido mucho estando enamorada, pero sabía perfectamente que no era feliz y que eso no era para mí. Esas relaciones tan turbulentas te vuelven un poco adicto, hay un enganche fuerte, pero creo que sabes que no es para ti. PABLO MOTOS. ¿Cómo eres cuando discutes en pareja? ESTER EXPÓSITO. A nadie tiene que venir alguien, que normalmente son hombres, a explicarle cómo tiene que ser feminista. -¿Qué personaje te gustaría hacer? - Tantas cosas… Así como más fantasía, diría que Catwoman, que además me encantan los gatos. articles.title: Comedian declares Jerry Seinfeld 'uncancellable' despite 'woke' anti-Israel festival boycott
articles.summary: Several performers pulled out of Lisbon's inaugural MEO Commedia a La Carte Fest after headliner Jerry Seinfeld's addition, citing support for the Palestinians.
articles.body: Several performers have pulled out of an international festival in Portugal headlined by comedian Jerry Seinfeld, with some citing concerns related to the Israel-Gaza conflict and others giving no public explanation. The withdrawals come ahead of the inaugural MEO Commedia a La Carte Fest in Lisbon, scheduled for Oct. 29 to Nov. 1. While some acts left the lineup without a public explanation, others cited political differences with performers involved in the festival. On Saturday, actress Inês Aires Pereira announced on Instagram that she was withdrawing her show Namastê from the festival lineup. In one image, Pereira wrote in Portuguese that "one of the names persistently defends ideas and acts that I consider indefensible. We cannot minimize or normalize a genocide," according to a translation by The Hollywood Reporter. COMEDIAN DECLARES HUGH LAURIE 'CAN'T BE CANCELED' AS ACTOR COMES TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S DEFENSE Musical comedy duo Cebola Mol also addressed their exit on Instagram, writing in a translated caption, "We will celebrate justice, freedom and joy with you on another occasion." The post included a cartoon watermelon, which is widely used as a symbol of Palestinian solidarity. Several departing acts did not disclose their motives. High-profile performers, including pop musical project Tributo Pop, comedian Pedro Tochas, the group Conjunto Cuca Monga and visual artist Vhils all withdrew from the festival lineup without publicly stating a reason. MICHAEL RAPAPORT SLAMS 'CLOWN' MACKLEMORE FOR ANTI-ISRAEL PERFORMANCE Seinfeld is the festival’s main headliner and has publicly supported Israel. The festival’s website still lists him as a performer. His support for Israel during the conflict has drawn accolades but also fierce criticism. In June, while leaving a New York Knicks game at Madison Square Garden, Seinfeld told a streamer asking for a "Free Palestine" shoutout that "it doesn’t exist." During an event at Duke University, Seinfeld also discussed pro-Palestinian protests, saying, "Free Palestine is, to me, just — you’re free to say you don’t like Jews. Just say you don’t like Jews. RABID ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVISTS SET TO HIT THE STREETS TONIGHT IN MAMDANI'S MANHATTAN "By saying ‘Free Palestine,’ you’re not admitting what you really think," he continued. "So, it’s actually — compared to the Ku Klux Klan, I’m actually thinking the Klan is actually a little better here because they can come right out and say, ‘We don’t like Blacks, we don’t like Jews.’ OK, that’s honest." Fox News Digital reached out to Seinfeld’s team but did not hear back. Comedian and media analyst Tim Young argued that the withdrawals hurt the departing performers far more than Seinfeld, whom he called "uncancellable." "It was a total eye-roll for me," said Young, who also serves as a Media Fellow at the Heritage Foundation and media editor at The Dallas Express. "I think anybody who is a comedian, anybody who is a performer, would want to work with basically the most successful, if not one of the most successful comedians in world history at this point. The guy's a billionaire from his comedy and his writing, and I don't know why you would want to walk away from it," he added. Young suggested the withdrawals were simply catering to their existing fan base, calling the move "a group of woke people performing for woke people." "They know who their audience is. They're behaving the way that their audience would behave and just playing into it," he said, adding the performers are likely getting more publicity from pulling out than they would have from performing. Young doesn't believe the withdrawals will have any lasting impact on Seinfeld's standing in the comedy world. BILL MAHER SAYS IT’S 'SO STUPID' FOR ANTI-TRUMP ARTISTS TO BAIL ON KENNEDY CENTER PERFORMANCES "You can’t cancel somebody like him," Young said. "Comedy is uncancellable. You get to a certain level, you're not going to be affected by it, and it’s important that people like Seinfeld … come out and say, ‘Hey, you know, this is bad, the things that are happening.' articles.title: Dolly Parton’s sister reveals ‘last thing’ country legend asked of her before death
articles.summary: Stella Parton said that prayer was the last thing her sister, Dolly Parton, asked for before her death from a brief battle with cancer.
articles.body: Dolly Parton's sister is sharing the final request she received from the musician. During a recent interview with "CBS Mornings," Stella Parton shared the last thing her sister asked of her before her death. "That’s the last thing Dolly asked me for, was prayer," she recalled. The legendary musician died Aug. 25 at the age of 80 after a "brief battle with cancer," which she hid from her fans and even some family members. DOLLY PARTON OFFERED TO TRY EXPERIMENTAL DRUGS IF ‘NO HOPE’ FOR CANCER BATTLE TO HELP OTHERS, SISTER SAYS Stella noted that the family would not be sharing what type of cancer Dolly had "out of respect for her" since Dolly "didn't tell us that we could say it." She added that she is able to speak about her love for her sister, but when it comes to her health, "it's not my business to tell her business." Concerns over the "Jolene" singer's health first arose in September 2025, when she made the difficult decision to postpone a number of shows in Las Vegas, telling fans she needed to undergo a "few procedures." "I want the fans and public to hear directly from me that, unfortunately, I will need to postpone my upcoming Las Vegas concerts," Parton shared online at the time. "As many of you know, I have been dealing with some health challenges, and my doctors tell me that I must have a few procedures." Shortly after Dolly made her announcement, concern among fans increased when her sister Freida asked fans to pray for Dolly, saying, "Many of you know she hasn’t been feeling her best lately." When speaking with "CBS Mornings," Stella noted, "I think Dolly got on to Freida about that. DOLLY PARTON’S ONGOING HEALTH BATTLE FORCES COUNTRY LEGEND TO MISS MAJOR DOLLYWOOD EVENT "I'm pretty sure Dolly said, 'You're going to, you know, pipe it down,' because that was the first time people thought 'Oh,'" she said. "And she knew that Freida was just upset and hurt, but she thought, 'Don't be telling my situation, Freida. Don't be spilling my business.'" According to Stella, Dolly decided to keep her diagnosis a secret because she "could not bear negative things" and didn't want her fans to worry about her. Her death came a little over a year after the death of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, who died in March 2025 at the age of 82. While some have speculated Dolly died of a broken heart, Stella doesn't agree. "I think she was very sad, but I don't think that's why she got sick," Stella said. "I think she worked too hard and didn't maybe take as good a care of herself as she should have. She, at one point, she said, 'You know, I spent a lot of time caring for Carl that maybe I neglected myself.'" DOLLY PARTON LAID TO REST AS NIECE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE TO ‘GRANNY’ She went on to say that while it "broke her heart to see him in the shape he" was in before he died, she ultimately believes Dolly's determination to continue working "so hard for so long" contributed to her death. When speaking about Dolly's relationship with Dean, she referred to it as "very unique and very deep and loyal" and gave Dean credit for being supportive of Dolly and loving "her enough to let her be what she was." Stella explained that while Dolly was a huge star across the globe, Dean "didn't care about that at all," and if it was up to him, she would have been "at the house with her hair up in a ponytail and barefooted cooking in the kitchen." Stella said even family members rarely saw Dolly without her signature glamorous look after she became a star. No. She would sleep in her makeup when she'd come spend the night with me," Stella said. "Oh, I knew what she looked like. She looked like me without her makeup. So, I knew what she looked like without it." Her sister also credited Dolly for being a good businesswoman, saying that while she had opinions on politics and other controversial topics, she never shared them because "she would never have offended anyone." Although Dolly was battling cancer, Stella says she knows her sister was at peace in her final moments. "She knew where she was going," she said. "She wasn't going anywhere bad. She was going to be with mom and daddy. She was prepared. Yeah, she was definitely prepared." articles.title: Liniker grava música de Caetano Veloso pela primeira vez para trilha de série | G1
articles.body:
Liniker dá voz à canção 'Dom de iludir' (1977) na trilha da série homônima que estreia neste segundo semestre de 2026 — Foto: Rony Hernandes / Divulgação 30e e b+ca

♬ Liniker gravou a canção “Dom de iludir”, composta por Caetano Veloso em diálogo com o samba-canção “Pra que mentir?”, música da primorosa parceria de Noel Rosa (1910 – 1937) com Oswaldo de Almeida Gogliano (1910 – 1962), o Vadico.

A canção “Dom de iludir” foi apresentada na voz de Maria Creuza em gravação feita para o álbum “Meia noite”, lançado em 1977, quarenta anos após a criação de “Pra que mentir?”, música composta em 1937 e lançada pelo cantor Silvio Caldas (1908 – 1998) em single editado em 1939.

Cinco anos depois da gravação de Maria Creuza, “Dom de iludir” ganhou a voz de Gal Costa (1945 – 2022) no álbum “Minha voz” (1982).

Liniker gravou a música para a trilha sonora de ainda inédita série da Netflix batizada com o nome da composição, abordada pelo autor Caetano Veloso duas vezes, ambas em gravações ao vivo dos álbuns “Totalmente demais” (1986) e “Noites do Norte ao vivo” (2001).

“Dom de iludir” é a primeira música de Caetano Veloso gravada por Liniker, mas os dois artistas já dividiram o palco em 2025 e, na ocasião, a cantora fez dueto com Caetano na canção “Sozinho” (Peninha, 1996).

articles.title: Rock in Rio: metrô, BRT e VLT terão operação especial até domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: Organização reforça o pedido para o uso do metrô combinado com o BRT. Jardim Oceânico terá embarque de madrugada, BRT Expresso terá 3 linhas e Linha 1 do VLT funcionará 24 horas.
articles.summary: Organização reforça o pedido para o uso do metrô combinado com o BRT. Jardim Oceânico terá embarque de madrugada, BRT Expresso terá 3 linhas e Linha 1 do VLT funcionará 24 horas.
articles.body:
Quem vai ao último fim de semana do Rock in Rio 2026, nesta sexta-feira (11), sábado (12) e domingo (13), terá um esquema especial de transporte público para chegar e voltar da Cidade do Rock. A Estação Jardim Oceânico do metrô ficará aberta 24 horas para embarque, o BRT terá três linhas especiais e a Linha 1 do VLT funcionará durante toda a madrugada .

Só nos quatro primeiros dias do festival, o BRT Expresso Rock in Rio transportou 152 mil passageiros. Foram 30 mil na sexta-feira (4), 35 mil no sábado (5), 47 mil no domingo (6) e 40 mil na segunda-feira (7).

“Nossa principal orientação para o público é que se programe antes de sair de casa, confira as opções de transporte e, faça a compra antecipadamente. Esse planejamento ajuda a tornar o deslocamento mais tranquilo e evita imprevistos na chegada e na saída da Cidade do Rock”, diz Gustavo Mostof, Diretor de Relações Institucionais do Rock in Rio.

Veja abaixo como funcionará cada meio de transporte no último fim de semana.

🚇 Metrô: Jardim Oceânico terá embarque de madrugada

A Estação Jardim Oceânico/Barra da Tijuca será o principal ponto de conexão do metrô com o esquema especial de BRT para a Cidade do Rock.

Na sexta (11) e no sábado (12), as linhas 1, 2 e 4 funcionarão normalmente das 5h à meia-noite . No domingo (13), o horário regular será das 7h às 23h .

Depois do encerramento da operação regular, o Jardim Oceânico continuará aberto para embarque durante a madrugada . As demais estações ficarão abertas apenas para o desembarque dos passageiros que deixarem o festival.

Na madrugada de domingo, a operação regular será retomada às 7h. Após o último dia do festival, as demais estações ficarão disponíveis para desembarque até as 5h de segunda-feira (14).

“A operação 24 horas do MetrôRio tem sido fundamental para organizar o deslocamento do público e oferecer uma forma ainda mais rápida, segura e confortável para quem vai ao festival. No primeiro fim de semana, tivemos uma operação muito positiva e, para os próximos dias, seguimos trabalhando para que os fãs possam chegar e voltar da Cidade do Rock com tranquilidade”, explica Gustavo Mostof, diretor de Relações Institucionais do Rock in Rio.

Durante a operação, as linhas 1 e 4 circulam entre Uruguai e Jardim Oceânico, enquanto a Linha 2 funciona entre Pavuna e Botafogo. A transferência entre as linhas 1 e 2 poderá ser feita no trecho compartilhado entre Central do Brasil/Centro e Botafogo.

A integração com o BRT Expresso Rock in Rio será feita pelo Terminal Jardim Oceânico .

🚌 BRT Expresso: três linhas levam à Cidade do Rock

O BRT Expresso Rock in Rio volta a operar nos dias 11, 12 e 13 de setembro, com três linhas especiais:

SE008: Terminal Jardim Oceânico x Terminal Centro Olímpico — serviço direto;

SE009: Terminal Alvorada x Estação Morro do Outeiro — serviço direto;

SE010: Terminal Paulo da Portela x Estação Morro do Outeiro — serviço semidireto, com paradas na Praça Seca, Tanque e Taquara.

O bilhete especial custa R$ 29 por pessoa e por dia e dá direito à ida e à volta — ou apenas ao retorno do festival.

A compra é feita pelo aplicativo Jaé , com o saldo da Conta Transporte, que pode ser carregada por Pix ou cartão de crédito. Não é possível comprar o bilhete usando saldo de Vale-Transporte.

Cada conta do Jaé pode comprar até dez bilhetes para cada dia do festival.

Para adquirir a passagem, o usuário deve entrar no aplicativo Jaé, selecionar “BRT Expresso Rock in Rio – venda”, clicar em “Comprar bilhete” , informar a quantidade de passageiros e o dia do festival e confirmar o pagamento.

O bilhete fica disponível em “Meus QRs” e o QR Code só é válido na data escolhida.

Atenção aos horários das estações próximas ao festival

Além da operação do BRT Expresso, algumas estações da região da Cidade do Rock terão horários específicos nos dias de festival:

Para quem fizer a combinação de metrô com o BRT Expresso Rock in Rio, a integração é feita exclusivamente no Jardim Oceânico. A estação Vicente de Carvalho não tem integração direta com o serviço especial.

O custo total para quem fizer ida e volta de metrô e usar o BRT Expresso é de R$ 44,80: R$ 15,80 pelos dois trechos de metrô e R$ 29 pelo serviço especial de BRT.

Na ida, o passageiro apresenta o QR Code para embarcar no BRT Expresso. Ao chegar ao Terminal Centro Olímpico ou à Estação Morro do Outeiro, será direcionado a uma tenda próxima à entrada da Cidade do Rock.

Ali, o QR Code será validado e o passageiro receberá uma pulseira individual , colocada no momento da validação. É essa pulseira que permitirá o embarque no serviço especial de volta . Ela é válida apenas para aquele dia do festival.

Quem quiser usar o BRT Expresso somente para voltar também precisará comprar o bilhete especial de R$ 29 pelo aplicativo Jaé.

Para ajudar no deslocamento depois dos shows, a Linha 1 do VLT, entre o Terminal Gentileza e o Santos Dumont, funcionará 24 horas nos dias 11, 12 e 13.

Entre 23h e 5h, haverá uma operação expressa, com trens circulando em intervalos de 60 minutos.

Nesse período, haverá embarque e desembarque somente nos seguintes pontos:

A partir das 5h, a Linha 1 retoma a operação regular, atendendo todas as paradas do trajeto.

As demais linhas do VLT funcionarão normalmente das 5h às 23h.

O esquema facilita principalmente a viagem de quem deixar o Rock in Rio de metrô e precisar seguir viagem pelo Centro. A integração com o VLT poderá ser feita nas estações Carioca e Cinelândia.

A Linha 1 também atende passageiros com destino à Rodoviária do Rio, ao Terminal Gentileza e ao Aeroporto Santos Dumont. No Gentileza, há conexões com linhas de ônibus e BRT.

A tarifa do VLT é de R$ 5. O pagamento pode ser feito com o cartão físico ou digital do Jaé.

No caso do cartão digital, o passageiro utiliza o aplicativo. Já o cartão físico pode ser adquirido nas máquinas de autoatendimento do Terminal Gentileza e das paradas e estações.

A passagem deve ser validada dentro do próprio VLT, aproximando o cartão do equipamento instalado próximo às portas.

Também é possível pagar diretamente por Pix. Nesse caso, o passageiro seleciona a opção “Pagar com Pix” no validador. O equipamento gera um QR Code, válido por 60 segundos, que deve ser escaneado pelo aplicativo do banco.

O passageiro deve guardar o comprovante e portar um documento de identidade durante a viagem para apresentá-los em caso de fiscalização.

Para quem sai de áreas atendidas pelo metrô, uma das opções é seguir de metrô até Jardim Oceânico e, de lá, pegar o BRT Expresso direto para o Terminal Centro Olímpico.

Na volta, o esquema funciona no sentido inverso: o passageiro pega o BRT especial próximo à Cidade do Rock e segue para o Jardim Oceânico. Mesmo após o fim da operação regular, será possível embarcar no metrô no Jardim Oceânico durante a madrugada e desembarcar nas demais estações.

Quem precisar seguir para pontos atendidos pelo VLT poderá fazer a conexão no Centro, com integração nas regiões das estações Carioca e Cinelândia. A Linha 1 continuará funcionando durante toda a madrugada, ligando o Centro ao Terminal Gentileza, à Rodoviária e ao Santos Dumont.

articles.title: Israeli film on Gaza receives 25-minute ovation at Venice premiere
articles.summary: Venice Film Festival honours NAZA, an expose on Israel’s use of AI systems in Gaza.
articles.body:
A film documenting Israel’s use of AI-powered systems to target Palestinians in Gaza has received a 25-minute standing ovation at its premiere at the Venice Film Festival.

The 80-minute film, NAZA, was directed by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, who won an Oscar in 2025 for No Other Land, a documentary on Israeli settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank, made with Palestinian co-directors Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal.

The result of a nearly three-year investigation, the film is built on testimony from Israeli military and intelligence sources who spoke on the condition that their identities be concealed. Their voices and faces were digitally altered, and they were filmed at night on Tel Aviv rooftops.

“We are letting the soldiers and the officers speak about what they did,” Abraham told the AFP news agency. “The goal was very simple: we wanted to hear, in as much detail as possible, how the systems of killing in Gaza looked, how they operated,” he added.

The film’s title is a Hebrew intelligence euphemism used to indicate the number of civilians expected to be killed in a given air strike. Interviewees describe an AI-assisted system known as “Lavender”, which drew on Gaza’s monitored telecommunications network – phone calls, movements and interactions – to identify assassination targets.

“It was done on a mass scale, like a factory,” one interviewee says in the film, while another involved in identifying targets says the process is “like a video game, because everything is done remotely” and is “insanely fun”.

Some interviewees spoke about the destruction of civilian homes, disregard for humanitarian law and a “general atmosphere” of “hatred” towards Palestinians.

“There can be no denying what intelligence personnel knew”, military sources in the film revealed, adding that they “witnessed with their own eyes and ears that the homes they were ‘incriminating’ were filled with families”.

Abraham said he hoped the film would push Western governments to drop their backing for Israel and apply pressure through sanctions.

“Those of us inside Israel and Palestine trying to fight for change need it. You are weakening the people inside who are supporting human rights and a political solution by refusing to act,” he told AFP, referring to Israel’s backers.

Writing jointly in +972 Magazine, Abraham and Szor said the film concluded that the killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza “was not a ‘tragic byproduct’ of a war against Hamas… but a premeditated, calculated, and intentional act”.

Screen International, a UK-based trade publication covering the global film industry, described the film as an “urgent, gut-punch”, while The Hollywood Reporter said it inspired “outrage… indignity as well. Most certainly disgust, on a profound level, for the current Israeli regime”.

The film was produced by the UK’s Jim Wilson with The Guardian, with executive producer Jonathan Glazer – the team behind The Zone of Interest, which won the 2024 Oscar for best international feature.

Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed about 73,500 Palestinians and wounded 174,500 since October 2023, according to Gaza’s Ministry of Health. Foreign journalists have been barred from entering Gaza except under tightly controlled conditions with the Israeli military.

NAZA is the only documentary in competition at this year’s festival, which concludes on Saturday, and follows last year’s The Voice of Hind Rajab, which received a 23-minute ovation and went on to win Venice’s second prize.

articles.title: Kunickaa Sadanand claims Poonam Dhillon and Padmini Kolhapure took papers from CINTAA office: 'This is a criminal offence' - WATCH
articles.summary: The ongoing dispute within the Cine and TV Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) has escalated, with allegations of documents being removed from the organisa.
articles.body: The ongoing dispute within the Cine and TV Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) has escalated, with allegations of documents being removed from the organisation’s office amid an ongoing legal battle and a court-ordered election.Speaking about the latest developments, Kunickaa Sadanand expressed deep disappointment over the situation in a video, saying, "I am very saddened to see the state of CINTAA today. I have never seen such behaviour from any committee in the last 40 years."Recounting the events, she said they were informed about the removal of documents from the office and rushed to the scene. She said in the video, "I was returning from the airport when I got a call from Manish Chaturvedi ji and Preeti ji. They told me that the CINTAA office, 'the previous committee, which is technically an illegal committee, is taking the papers in a hurry. You should reach there immediately'. They reached the police station."According to Kunickaa, the matter was taken to the police, who allegedly said that they could not prevent the removal of the documents without an order from the Charity Commissioner. "The police said that 'we cannot stop them. You should get an order from the Charity Commission'. It is obvious that we will have to go to the Charity Commission tomorrow to get an order. We will have to give an application to them, but till then, whatever tampering has to be done… I am not saying that they are going to tamper, but why were they taking the papers? What was their need? This creates a doubt as to why they transported the papers from our court CINTAA office. They were sending it to the office in Kartik Complex. The tempo went there."Sadanand further alleged that people associated with the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) intervened and stopped the vehicle carrying the documents. "Luckily, the people of FWICE stopped the tempo they put the papers in CINTAA's office and put a lock on it. When all this was going on, we even asked the police, that when they showed you the papers and everything, why did you let it go? The police said that 'It is not in our hands.' We also explained to them that this is a public trust office and this is CINTAA's office. These people are entering there illegally. They are not supposed to be in the office. They have no access to any paper, to any account."She further noted that the removal or handling of documents amounted to tampering, particularly with an election having already been ordered by the courtIn her video, she claimed that there was video footage showing several individuals "were loading papers in Poonam ji's car. We took a video of that and then asked the police to stop them."The member said the police temporarily stopped the process and examined documents. "After that, they said, 'These are our court papers.' With great difficulty, the police showed us those papers. Some of those were court papers, but the next hearing is on the 16th, so let them be, you lock them up." She added, "The police also suggested that you lock them up and keep the keys with you. But still, they did not listen.""I don't know which ministers have been called, because the police officers were not listening to us. And this is very wrong. We are going to take very serious action," she added.Revealing Padmini Kolhapure's alleged explanation for taing away the documents, she said, "Padmini ji said, 'I am taking the papers for safeguarding.' Who are you safeguarding from? There are so many people sitting here. Will they let anyone steal?"She also alleged that there was an altercation, adding, "Poonam ji tried to snatch his phone and break it. We held her hand. Poonam ji was not allowing us to take a video. We told her, 'Poonam ji, we can't expect this from you'."She went on to add, "The police allowed us to put a lock on a carton of papers they had kept in a room. And on top of that, because the lock system was different, we took a video of it. And the locking system that was on top, we put some tape on it."Concluding the statement, she said, "I just want to tell you that I am very saddened. The great artists who established CINTAA could never have imagined that this day would come. I mean, I haven't seen members of the committee behave like this for 40 years."Former CINTAA General Secretary Upasana Singh alleged that the Cine and TV Artistes Association (CINTAA) committee had been dissolved after 11 members resigned, claiming that the formation of a new committee was against the association's constitution.Singh said that as per CINTAA's constitution, the committee stands dissolved if 50 per cent or more members resign.A press briefing was held regarding the ongoing constitutional crisis within CINTAA and the need to restore democratic functioning through fresh elections.According to the press release, 8 out of 15 elected members of the CINTAA Executive Committee resigned, resulting in more than 50 per cent of the elected positions becoming vacant. Under Clause 18(F)(iii) of the CINTAA Constitution, the Executive Committee consequently stands dissolved, and fresh elections are required.Upasna Singh has approached FWICE seeking its intervention to ensure free, fair and transparent elections.The release also raises concerns over former President Poonam Dhillon and former Vice President Padmini Kolhapure allegedly continuing to convene meetings, issue communications and pass resolutions despite the dissolution of the Executive Committee.The press release highlights concerns over lack of transparency, collective decision-making and democratic functioning within CINTAA.Upasna Singh stated that the issue is not a battle between individuals but a fight to protect CINTAA's Constitution, democratic governance and the rights of its members, and called for fresh elections under FWICE supervision.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
